points.content: The Halcyon archive re-ingest stalled at 62 percent because of a duplicate-processing race, not throughput or starvation
The retry loop added in the batch runner bypassed the batch ownership check, so no lease rows existed and two workers could claim the same batch
Each batch must claim a single-owner lease row before processing, and the claim is the only thing that can complete it
A distributed lock service is rejected; a simple lease row with an expiry is enough
The lease row is keyed by batch id with a thirty-second expiry and a compare-and-swap update on completion
The losing worker retries the batch after a sixty-second backoff rather than dropping it, because losing the batch silently is how events are lost
An expired lease with no completion makes the batch claimable again, giving crash recovery for free
The completion path needs the owner check; nothing else changes
The lease change must ship before the October 15 freeze, with no scope creep
The wire queue processes batches of five thousand events each, and the lease round-trip budgets roughly a second per batch
The Halcyon re-ingest covers about twelve million events, or twenty-four hundred batches end to end
At a second per batch with four workers the re-ingest is about ten minutes of pure processing, well inside the maintenance window
The backfill cutoff is fixed at September 30 so the re-ingest covers only the outage window and does not re-ingest events that already landed
The backfill cutoff is added as a constant so the next backfill does not guess at it
The lease-table migration is additive — a new lease table with an index on batch id — and should land before Friday's 2am DB maintenance window to avoid interaction with the vacuum job
Maya Chen owns the ingest queue service now, having taken it over when the old platform group split, and will be cc'd on the PR
Tomas is the escalation contact for queue internals if the stall recurs, rather than paging the whole team
The hydrate stage was audited and found clean, so the lease change is scoped to the wire queue
The stall was in the wire stage, where four workers ran at full CPU while the queue depth barely moved
No lease rows existed at all while every worker was actively processing batches
The staging cluster runs the latest release, so the stall is not a stale deploy artifact
Every worker was retrying the same handful of batches in a loop, visible in the logs
Two workers grabbed the same batch twice from the ingest queue and each marked its own copy complete
The DB maintenance window is Friday at 2am

points.content: lumen auth is migrating from team-scoped tokens to per-graph API keys so each graph gets its own credential and its own audit trail
The team signed off on the per-graph API key direction last Friday
A per-graph key encodes the graph id rather than the team id, so the registry can route a key back to its graph without a lookup
The platform standard is the tt_ prefix with a random 32-byte secret after it
Every graph key starts with tt_ and nothing else in the system may mint that prefix
Every graph key has a token lifetime of twenty-four hours with rotation on the boundary
Short-lived graph keys mean a leak is a one-day problem rather than a quarterly audit finding
Legacy team keys remain valid until the rotation window closes, but no new ones are minted from the day of the flip
Forcing every team to rotate on day one would break the pilot
Bluepeak Logistics is the pilot customer for the per-graph rollout; their integration team is small and they were already asking for scoped credentials
Priya owns the registry service, inherited with the data platform handoff
Priya will be looped into the interface review before the resolver is touched
The registry must move from a team-scoped resolver to a graph-scoped resolver
A revoked key presented mid-request fails closed with a 401 and no fallback to team scope
A revoked key must be dead on the next request, otherwise the audit story falls apart
Key usage events are kept for ninety days, same as the rest of the audit log
Anything shorter than ninety days of key usage retention cannot answer the incident questions we get asked
The deploy is two-phase: phase one mints graph keys with enforcement off, phase two flips enforcement after the sandbox org runs on them for a week
A single-commit flip across issuance, resolution, and enforcement was judged too risky
The only remaining team-token assumption in lumen is the admin settings page, which renders the team token
The admin settings page will be replaced with a per-graph key table

The quarterly demo is next Tuesday

The duplicate-processing race is scope-independent once the lease is held: rollout scope does not change the guarantee

points.content: the global flag's cutover flip raced lease renewal, leaving a renewal window where two workers could claim one batch
the global flag was toggled once at cutover and never touched after
the toggle was two hours before the first duplicate and the renewal stamps were clean with no overlap or double renewal
clock skew between regions can make lease expiry unsafe: a lagging region renews after the owner's lease truly expired and its renewal can clobber a live lease in another region
the flag did not cause the duplicates; it had been stable for two hours before the anomaly
the Bluepeak region clock drifted eleven seconds, which is exactly the six-minute duplicate window on the hydrate queue

the lease behaved as designed under a drifted clock: expiry is compared against wall-clock time, so a lagging region's clock expired the lease early, a second worker claimed the batch, and the hydrate side saw the duplicate
the fix is not about the flag at all; a skew-tolerant lease needs a grace period on the expiry check so a lagging region cannot clobber a live lease
eleven seconds is the worst logged inter-region skew, while the SLO review had assumed sub-second
the lease expiry grace period is sized to thirty seconds, with any expiry landing inside the grace window logged internally
the thirty-second grace bounds the skew hazard without making the lease lax
the skew-tolerant lease grace period shipped to every region, so a lagging region's renewal can no longer clobber a live lease and the clock-skew risk is covered
the all-at-once rollout call is reversed for the next rollout: per-service flags replace the single global flag
the global flag made one bad region a fleet-wide event and has been the single point of failure all along
per-service flags change the reversibility model: each service's flag is pulled independently rather than one fleet-wide switch
the skew fix ships with a hydrate queue re-run before the next rollout
Priya will track the grace-expiry log for a week
the all-at-once rollout call had been second-guessed since it was made, before the Bluepeak anomaly

mitigations.content: [MITIGATION] the skew-tolerant lease grace period shipped to every region, so a lagging region's renewal can no longer clobber a live lease and the clock-skew risk is covered
